bugs.text: Fatal crash right after pressing Enter: e.anim is only set inside updEnemies, which does not run during 'stStart', so drawEnemy indexes SPR.zako[undefined] and drawSpr reads .width of undefined. The exception escapes loop() before requestAnimationFrame is re-queued, so the game freezes on a star-only frame forever (confirmed by result.json error at 4.1 s and identical screenshots 2..5).

Escort Goei crash: when their boss finishes the dive or dies, startReturn reads e.path.p3.x, but an escort's path is its entry/return path (endSlot, no p3), so it throws a TypeError and would kill the loop the first time a boss dives with escorts.
Challenging-stage hit counting never implemented: G.ch.hits / G.ch.killed are never incremented, so the 1,000 wave bonus and 10,000 PERFECT never trigger and NUMBER OF HITS always shows 0.
Challenging-stage enemies score formation values (50/80/150) instead of 100 each.
Stage badges are 1-6 identical flags by threshold, not arcade denominations; stages 1-4 all show one flag.
Results screen omits shots fired; ramming an enemy counts as a hit (412).
Capture has no pull-up animation (captive appears instantly) and the freed fighter falls straight down and docks wherever the player is.
SND.hit is defined but never played.
Title screen: 'x ESCORT' overlaps the 160 value and the controls line is clipped at both sides (screenshot 1-title).
Ram hitbox is taller than the sprites.

summary: A compact, mostly well-organised clone whose code covers most of the spec on paper: integer-scaled 3:4 canvas, twinkling starfield, correct 40-enemy formation with bezier entries, sway and breathing, curved dives that re-enter from the top, escorts with 400/800/1600 scoring, a widening tractor beam, captive/rescue/dual-fighter logic and Web Audio sounds. But it never gets past the title screen: the first rendered frame after Enter throws because the wing-flap frame index is set only by the enemy update, which does not run during the STAGE intro, and the exception kills the requestAnimationFrame loop for good, as the play-test confirms (frozen star-only frames, no movement). Even with that fixed, a second crash waits in the escort return path, challenging-stage hits and bonuses are never counted, badges ignore the arcade denominations, and capture/rescue are simplified. Tidy but terse code. The faithfulness to Galaga is in the design only, never in play.
